literature.title: Literature
literature.lead: We consider Charles Butler's *The Feminine Monarchie* through a historical and literary lens, its publication history, and its impact on the understanding of bees and beekeeping in the context of 17th-century Britain.

music.title: Music
music.lead: From the simple notation of a bee's tooting in the 1609 edition, to the fully fledged 'Melissomelos' included in the 1623 *The Feminine Monarchie*, we explore Butler's musical understanding of bees and its relationship to the broader musical landscape of the time. Inspired by Butler's pioneering work, we also extend into musical explorations of our own.

science.title: Science
science.lead: Butler's *The Feminine Monarchie*, in addition to its importance to beekeeping in Britain, is also a significant work in the history of science. Butler's understanding of bees was groundbreaking — he was the first describe the queen bee and her role in the hive. Inspired by Butler's pioneering work, we extend his understanding of emotions in bees and investigate the role of mood in bee behaviour.

connections.title: Connections
connections.lead: Connections is the place were we, as a team, reflect on the points of contact and divergence between the different sections of the project. It is also the space where we connect to organisations and people from outside of our project whose work touches on the themes we explored through *The Feminine Monarchie*.

about.title: About
about.lead: This experimental project, funded by the [Leverhulme Trust](https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/), is a collaboration between artists and humanists (composition, literary studies, musicology), scientists (biology, psychology, animal cognition), and a research software engineer, who came together to explore historical and contemporary approaches to the study of bee 'sentience', and create a digital bee book that could contain our different research findings.
